note: Cell values are in moon_base.bin at position cell_id. A 1-degree polar cell is a strip that averages lit and shadowed ground (feature_vs_cell).

sites.name: Shackleton
sites.why: south-polar rim: highly illuminated rim, shadowed interior (solar/ice)
sites.site_note: crater centre; the lit rim and the PSR floor share the cell
sites.feature_vs_cell: polar cell: 30.3 km north-south by only 0.26 km east-west, a strip that cuts across rims, slopes and floors; the value averages lit and shadowed ground along it

sites.why: most illuminated south-polar site in Glaser et al. 2014 (92.27 % at 2 m, 95.65 % at 10 m)
sites.site_note: not an IAU name and no coordinates in the cited sources (R2 notes): no cell assigned. It lies between the Shackleton and de Gerlache rows above; its sub-km ridge crest cannot be seen in any 1-degree value (cell illum_frac is a strip average, ~0.06-0.15 here).
